title: Relational Identity and the Bones of the Soul
english: This is understood by those making progress: that they have labored to possess something, but not perfectly. For what is the difference between 'upon the Lord' and 'in the Lord'? One who takes the prepositions unskillfully will say there is no difference. But it can be so: for instance, someone is rejoiced upon his child if he is healthy, but rejoiced in a drink of wine. He has a different cause for each.

Let us take the proof from another word: 'everyone' (as he says), 'who confesses in me in the presence of men' (Romans 10:10)—he did not say 'upon me'—'and I will confess him.' If the preposition had been placed simply, 'in' would have been placed even in the denial: 'and everyone denying in me, I will deny in him' (Matthew 10:33). But it was impossible 'to be denying in Christ' the one denying him, or for Christ to deny the one existing in him. Therefore, the one denying has been severed. The one who denies God has been severed, and his God has turned away. But the one confessing him is in him, so that you may not receive the confession by voice alone; for those honoring with lips confess, but they are not in him.

Since, therefore, our connection to God is also different, at times we say we rejoice upon him as upon a savior, as upon a benefactor, as upon a general who has secured the victory for us, but at other times 'in him' as in wisdom, as in sanctification, as in righteousness. The one confessing, therefore, is in Christ. And take from another example: one confessing knowledge cannot confess it otherwise than if he knew it.

But if so, is it as in essence or in quality? Let these things be left for later; for now the inquiry is about the difference of the prepositions. Whether one participates in essence or in quality, let it be at another time. And the same: for God is not a different Father becoming of the righteous, a different Creator of them, or a different King of them, in thought. From which we take the thoughts, since there is not in it a distribution of thought from thought. God is light, and is also sanctification and righteousness and wisdom, and it is not possible to separate existence from existence. But we separate relation from relation. Let a man be father and master and teacher and ruler; for he does not differ from himself. If, however...

You may hear that a ruler is [a ruler] in relation to those being ruled, and a king in relation to those being kinged, and a father in relation to the one born, and a master in relation to the slave, and a physician in relation to the one being treated, and a teacher in relation to the one learning; it is not the person himself in relation to himself that makes the difference, but the relation which is directed toward one other and another that makes the distinction. Just as it happens to the same person to be both father and teacher and the others, it also happens for the same disciple to be to the ruler and to the learner. Again, since one is not always said in relation to one—for it happens to find a son of another and the same one to be a disciple of another and a friend of another—9 he will be delighted in his salvation. Regarding 'salvation' here he means 'salvation'; for often 'salvation' signifies 'salvation'. And there is a case where even the agent of salvation is called thus, as if he were saying: 'The ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God' (Ps 18:45), instead of 'the Savior.' Therefore the soul 'is delighted' in 'the salvation.' It does not seek salvation from elsewhere than from this God, from Him, eternal salvation from the one saving; for 'Israel' 'is saved by the Lord with eternal salvation' (Ps 106:1).

10 'All my bones shall say, Lord, Lord, who is like you?' (Ps 62:11). First, it is theology to know what the holiness of God is and who is able or unable to be made like Him. Therefore apply this theology and the knowledge of God to your own bones, from which it appears that he is not speaking about his own bones, those which hold together the other members of the body and the flesh and the nerves, but about the agile powers, of which we have often said that they are the bones of the inner man. Therefore 'all' 'my bones shall say'; the agile doctrines, my agile movements, according to which I recognize and understand, confess God, that no one of the created things happens to be like Him. Furthermore: the 'who' [refers to] how? —in the context of the impossible, as in: 'God, who shall be like you?'; regarding the Son we do not take this [to mean likeness in the future]; for he does not have the likeness in what is to come, but being the 'character of the substance' he is eternally like. Therefore two things can be taken: if concerning likeness of essence, no one is made like Him. But if concerning [likeness] according to virtue and holiness, he who is made like Him is rare.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Purpose of Goodness and the Sackcloth of Repentance
english: Him. Rescuing the poor from the hands of those stronger than he. If the similarity is taken regarding this action, the verse signifies: God rescues the poor and the needy from the hands of those stronger than him. And this is over men, such as rulers, powerful in strength, and also the devil himself. Therefore, only God rescues from these. If, however, as I have said, he is rescued from practical matters, the verse is also able to do this; for it is not a great thing to rescue from lesser things. Those remaining according to Sosannas seemed to be stronger than her; for they were rulers and judges, but that woman was a chambermaid and a private person. And God rescued from the stronger. And this is to be understood: everyone who is of some lesser strength is poor according to this, the one unable to benefit himself, the one not able to help himself and to make himself out of the surrounding circumstance. And poor and needy from those seizing him. And it happens especially according to the underlying subject to be both poor and needy. If he is outside of wealth, he is poor; but if he is satisfied by his toil, he is a needy man; for 'the rich have become poor' (Job 22:28). If, therefore, you lift these things up, you take the man from the Jews who believed to be the poor, and the needy as one not having hope, but also being godless.

Unjust witnesses arose, things which they did not know, they questioned me. The unjust witnesses question him about things which the one whom they wish to testify against does not know. Here, 'things which they did not know', [is] 'things which they were not tested'. The name of not knowing sometimes signifies ignorance; 'but at that time not knowing God', it declares ignorance. It also signifies not having been tested, as if I say: 'the one not knowing sin', the one not having been tested by sin. Therefore, he knows her according to something; he understands her nature. But he does not know her without having used her. Thus also regarding wives and women in general, it is said that: 'he did not know her', 'he knew her'. He signifies the experience here. 'And Adam knew Eve his wife' (Gen 4:1). This was said when they had come together; for he approached: 'and having come together, she bore' (Gen 4:1). Therefore, the unjust ones are witnesses who say against someone things which are not present to him. Such also is this: 'as the evil was turning away from me, he did not know'. Repay me evil for good, and barrenness to my soul (Ps 31:11). It was necessary for him...

They did not realize that I was not being kind to them, nor did they know what I am asking; for I was about to be punished, and because of this, not only will they not be punished for me, but as much as it concerns me. Thus we also interpreted the Gospel: 'Be well-disposed toward your adversary until you are with him in the way' (Matt 5:44).

And since the word of well-disposition is this: 'Well-disposition is a will of good things for the sake of the neighbor,' for many times I desire to provide good things to him in order to gain something from him. Therefore, they wanted to punish me, who had done them no wrong, but had also provided them an opportunity for salvation. Such also is what is said by Jacob to Laban: 'Know, if there is anything of yours with me, take it' (Gen 31:32). I do not want any of yours; I am well-disposed toward you, I give back to you the things. Instead of the good things which I did for them, I have done good things to them so that they would not be established for the sake of being punished because of me, since I did not show them.

Even Susanna would not have said concerning the elders: 'They intended to tear me away to adultery; I was not well-disposed toward them; I did a good thing to them; as far as it concerns me, they have not committed in sin to make me barren' (Sus 3:7)? The 'they repaid me' is common; just as they repaid me evil instead of good, so also they repaid my soul with barrenness. And what about the offspring of the soul? Right thoughts, excellent deeds. 'From the fear of you we conceived in the womb and labored and brought forth' (Ps 22:3).

And I, while they were bothering me, was putting on sackcloth. Behold, their evils and the reason for wanting to make her barren—they bothered her by name, as the one who said, 'sophistical disturbances bother me more than they harm me.' However, I was putting on sackcloth so that, not being abandoned, I would not be captured by them, and on their behalf so that they would cease their insolence toward me; I was putting on a certain strict life, bearing in some way a sign of repentance, so that I might not be harmed by the bothering, and on the other hand, so that they might not be emboldened. And it is much more for the good, if they should cease. And they humbled my soul in fasting (Ps 35:6). I was not putting on sackcloth alone, that is, strictness of life, but also 'they humbled my soul in fasting,' both according to the literal sense and according to the original sense, no longer being nourished by those painful things.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Humiliation of the Apostle
english: And the use of history often happens for assistance; for we have seen many things accomplished through fasting, such as the city of Nineveh not falling to destruction, and the nation of the Jews being saved from Haman. 'And my prayer shall turn into my bosom' (Ps 17:5). By the name of the bosom, in many writings, the governing principle and the mind are signified, as if it says: 'everything shall turn into the bosom of the unrighteous.' It is equal to: 'I have given their ways into their own heads' (Ps 106:15); for again the heads signify the governing principle: 'his labor shall return upon his own head.' The holy man prays that good things might come to be. And there is no other prayer than a 'petition for good things from God.' When someone obtains the good things for which he prayed, his prayer was turned into his own bosom. It was not cast away and remained outside, whose voice was sent up and was scattered into the air, but it brought what he had asked. And this means that his prayer is not sent up in vain, but is received into the heart of the one praying, into what he asked: 'the one filling your desire with good things.' The one desiring them is filled with them. 'This deception is in the land of Egypt, in their bosom' (Gen 41:54). And: 'the woman who is in your bosom,' whom you love, who is of one mind with you, who is in agreement with you. 'And my prayer shall turn into my bosom.' The one asking good things from God prays. When he obtains what he asks, his prayer turned into his bosom, into his governing principle. And I have diverted from many sayings, that the governing principle is often signified by the name of the bosom: 'this is their deception in the land of Egypt in their bosom.' And again: 'everything comes into the bosom of the unrighteous.'

But the bosom signifies intimacy. So also in the bosoms [of the patriarchs] Abraham found rest, having the same courage and endurance, and: 'the woman who is in your bosom,' your own, living together with you. As a neighbor, as our brother, thus they were pleasing. This says that: no one has an excuse to be angry with me, no one takes from me a cause to be an enemy to me; for toward each one I was thus as a neighbor, as a brother, and thus they were pleasing through brotherly love, friendship, and sibling-love. As one mourning and dejected.

Living, thus I was humbled. 'Thus I was humbled' because of them. Those whom it seemed to be neighbors and brothers were gathered against me; they waged war against me, as in the beginning of this psalm: 'Judge, O Lord, those doing wrong to me, fight those fighting against me' (Ps 54:5). Again he says: 'To me they spoke peace, but they were plotting deceit in anger' (Ps 55:21). Because of this, as one mourning them and as one being gloomy toward them, thus I was humbled; for if I were providing them with things that gladden, I would be exalted, rejoice, and be glad from cheerfulness.

But what about 'thus I was humbled'?—if someone has a son whom he loves and desires, and sees him burning, he is humbled, because not as he wished him to live, thus he sees him suffering evil. Since therefore I was providing opportunities for virtue as toward neighbors and brothers, but they themselves were proving to be enemies and foes, I was humbled toward them, though it was necessary for me to rejoice toward them. What do you think of Paul concerning Hymenaeus and Alexander, was he not humbled seeing them shipwrecked concerning the faith? Was it not previously thus toward them, that he did not love, did not give opportunities toward blessedness? And if these things are said regarding the face of the Savior, he is able to say these things regarding Judas and regarding the whole people of the Hebrews. And they rejoiced against me and were gathered together.

But do you wish to know that the descent upon one sinning is humiliation? Paul writes to the Corinthians, stirring them up toward repentance, he says: 'Lest coming I should find you and my God should humble me' (1 Cor 4:14). The holy man is exalted when he sees those being helped by him becoming better. And a father, having rejoiced over children and being glad, is exalted. If I had been preserving the love which I was preserving toward them, toward me, I would not have been humbled, but I would have been exalted, having such as equals, having sharers. 'And they rejoiced against me and were gathered together.' But I was thus toward them from most private compassion; but they, from the opposite, having been gathered against me, rejoiced or, having rejoiced against me, were gathered together, in order that they might bring more evil and misery to me. Scourges were gathered against me, and I did not know. The eagerness is to do evil. I said in the previous readings from one of the psalms, that the same evils are to some as scourges, and to others as contests, when...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
